why: I checked all five expect lines and their proofs. Each one can be checked by running something on the PR head. Line 1 writes /tmp/cfgcheck/broken.json, runs `node src/app.js` on it, then checks that the exit code is 1, stdout has 0 bytes and stderr contains the path. Line 2 greps that same stderr for `line 3` or `broken.json:3`, using an exact regex, so there is only one answer. Line 3 uses a node one-liner that must print OK. It checks that loadConfig throws and that the error message contains the path. Line 4 checks the regression case with deepEqual plus the `listening on 9000` output and exit 0. Line 5 runs `npm test` and then reads test/ for a test that asserts the path appears in the error, which a careful reader can confirm. Nothing depends on a release, a deploy or a published page. Everything works with local files and the repo's own code.
